findings.desc: signing-guard-mutation-proof-smoke.ts proves guard removal by regex-matching the SIGNABLE_SESSION_SOURCES Set literal in the COMPILED dist artifact (topology-critic-receipt.js), then mutating a copy in a temp dir. This is verified SAFE (real artifact is read-only throughout; mutation writes only to a fresh mkdtemp path cleaned in a finally block; byte-identical check at the end confirms no residue) and the brittleness is bounded (assert.ok(match) at line 25 fails loudly, not silently, if the build output shape ever changes the Set literal formatting) -- but it is still coupled to esbuild/tsc output formatting (e.g. quote style, whether the Set literal stays inline vs gets split across lines by a future compiler/minifier change) rather than to TS source AST. A more robust alternative would regex/parse the TS SOURCE (topology-critic-receipt.ts) instead of dist, or use a source-level import + monkey-patch of the Set at runtime instead of string surgery on compiled output. Not blocking: the current test passes, fails loudly on drift, and the constraint (prove BUILT guard removal without recompiling) is a real one under time pressure. Recording as advisory since a finding is more useful than a pass here.
findings.resolvedReason: Duplicate of B-49ed:F-002. Same regex-brittleness observation, recorded first with agent=main because the reviewer's shell lacked PROOF_OR_STOP_AGENT on its initial attempt, so the finding misattributed to the main agent rather than to lattice-review-quality. F-002 is the authoritative record with correct reviewer attribution and a valid reviewRunId binding. Keeping this row rather than deleting it, since the misattribution itself is worth seeing in the audit trail.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/signing-guard-mutation-proof-smoke.ts:23-25,50 proves guard removal by regex-matching the SIGNABLE_SESSION_SOURCES Set literal in the COMPILED dist artifact (dist/core/topology-critic-receipt.js) and mutating a COPY in a fresh mkdtemp dir. Verified safe: the real dist file is only read (never written), the mutant is written only under the mkdtemp scratch dir which is rmSync-cleaned in a finally block, and the test itself asserts byte-identical restoration at the end (confirmed empirically by re-running the smoke: PASS, and diffing the real dist file before/after -- unchanged). The brittleness the author flagged is real but bounded, not silent: assert.ok(match, ...) at line 25 fails LOUDLY if the build output ever changes the Set literal formatting (e.g. minification, multi-line reformat), because the guard-presence check at line 21 and the set-literal regex at line 24 both run before any mutation; a shape change breaks the proof-of-concept itself rather than letting a weakened guard through silently. Suggestion (non-blocking): parsing/matching the TS SOURCE (topology-critic-receipt.ts) instead of the compiled dist output would decouple the proof from build-tool formatting choices, at the cost of not proving the SHIPPED artifact contains the guard. Recording as a finding rather than a pass per reviewer instruction; this is advisory, not a blocker.
findings.resolvedReason: Fair advisory. signing-guard-mutation-proof-smoke regex-matches a Set literal in the COMPILED dist artifact, which is brittle: if the build output shape changes, the regex stops matching. Accepted rather than fixed because the smoke asserts the guard call site is present BEFORE attempting the mutation, so a shape change fails loudly at that assertion rather than silently passing a proof that no longer proves anything. The reviewer independently confirmed this ordering. Parsing the TS source instead of dist would be more robust and is worth doing if this proof is ever generalised beyond the single Set literal it targets.

findings.desc: CHK-002 userSees claims 'no test sets LATTICE_SESSION_ID to establish a signing identity', but at least 24 files under packages/main/src/tasks/ still directly assign process.env.LATTICE_SESSION_ID (or set it as a literal in an env object) to establish a signing/owner identity for CLI invocations under test, e.g. decision-doc-promotion-smoke.ts:48, delivery-context-pack-smoke.ts:482/489, evidence-refresh-smoke.ts:374/381, done-required-validation-smoke.ts:321/329, live-smoke-transcript-smoke.ts:827/1178/1185, frozen-claim-snapshot-hook-smoke.ts:70, plan-skeleton-smoke.ts:224/231, checklist-reload-hint-smoke.ts:64, proofstory-acceptance-basis-smoke.ts:68. This is the exact CHK-002 scope stated in plan.md (167 lines/29 files under packages/main/src/tasks/), and 29 files still contain the literal today. Since these tests dispatch/CLI-invoke under an explicit-env session id, any of them that exercise deriveRoleProvenance-gated commands would now hit the new CHK-001 guard and fail (or were silently routed around it), not migrated per plan. Fix: either complete the migration through the shared adapter-session-env.ts helper for all remaining files, or narrow CHK-002 userSees/scope to the subset actually migrated and file a follow-up for the rest.
findings.resolvedReason:
The finding is correct and the defect is mine: CHK-002 userSees says 'no test sets LATTICE_SESSION_ID to establish a signing identity', and 29 files under packages/main/src/tasks still contain the literal. That promise as written is false.

What I verified before resolving: NONE of those 29 files invoke a deriveRoleProvenance-gated command. I grepped every file containing LATTICE_SESSION_ID for topology_critic_receipt_set and topology_exclusion_approval_set and got zero hits. So none of them reach the CHK-001 guard, none were silently routed around it, and the suite does not fail because of them. The migrated set is exactly the two files that DO reach the guard (proofstory-topology-critic-smoke, proofstory-pre-review-check-smoke), which is what CHK-001 required.

Of the 29 remaining, 74 of the occurrences are in story-owner-lease-smoke.ts, which exists specifically to ASSERT explicit-env session semantics (it asserts sessionSource === 'explicit-env' at lines 200 and 621). Migrating that file would destroy the assertions it exists to make, so it must NOT be migrated. The remainder are thinly spread across files that use the env var for ordinary owner-lease identity in CLI invocations, unrelated to receipt signing.

So the code is correct and the promise is over-broad. I cannot edit the userSees text because the checklist is frozen from INIT_CHECK onward and I am the executor. Recording this as partially_mitigated rather than fixed, with the residual scope carried to a follow-up rather than silently narrowed: the accurate claim is 'no test that reaches a signing-guarded command establishes identity via LATTICE_SESSION_ID', and the broader cleanup of non-signing fixtures is separate work with no security consequence.

findings.desc: CHK-003 userSees names the wrong smoke as its acceptance criterion: it says 'proofstory-topology-critic-smoke reports PASS, and reverting the CHK-001 guard makes it fail with an assertion naming the forgeable session source'. Running packages/main/dist/tasks/proofstory-topology-critic-smoke.js today exits 1 on an assertion at basis.status (expected complete, actual partial) that is unrelated to the signing-source guard and pre-existing (the file is byte-identical to main before this story touched it, per git diff main..HEAD~1 vs main). It never reaches the session-source guard or exclusion-approval code paths, so it cannot report PASS and cannot demonstrate the mutation-revert behaviour userSees describes. The actual verificationEvidence recorded for CHK-003 correctly points to two DIFFERENT, newly-added files instead (topology-signing-source-guard-smoke.ts and signing-guard-mutation-proof-smoke.ts, both of which do pass and do prove the guard mechanically), so the guard itself is adequately proven -- but the userSees text is stale/inaccurate and still promises an outcome the code does not produce. Fix: update CHK-003 userSees to name topology-signing-source-guard-smoke / signing-guard-mutation-proof-smoke (the tests actually used), not proofstory-topology-critic-smoke.
findings.resolvedReason:
Accurate: CHK-003's userSees names proofstory-topology-critic-smoke as the pass criterion, but that smoke exits 1 on a pre-existing basis.status assertion unrelated to this story. I verified this independently by checking out main's version of that file in place, running it with tsx, observing the same failure, then restoring mine byte-identical. So the failure predates this story and is not a regression.

Accepted rather than fixed because the checklist is frozen from INIT_CHECK onward and I am the executor, so I cannot edit the userSees text. The recorded verificationEvidence already points at the two smokes that DO pass and mechanically prove the guard (topology-signing-source-guard-smoke, signing-guard-mutation-proof-smoke), so the evidence chain is sound even though the userSees prose names a stale target. The reviewer reached the same conclusion: 'the guard itself is fine, only the userSees text is stale.'

findings.desc: The scope-plan exclusion approver call site (proofstory.ts:550) is a bound signing role identical in risk profile to the critic (:565), per this story's own decision rationale, but its LEGITIMATE (accepted-session) path through topology_exclusion_approval_set is never exercised end to end anywhere in the current test suite. Its only production call sites in tests are inside proofstory-topology-critic-smoke.ts (lines ~505/538 for the negative/rejected cases, and the one positive-path call implied by the test flow), and that whole smoke test currently exits 1 at an assert.equal(basis.status, 'complete') check (see F-004) BEFORE it ever reaches the exclusion-approval flow. So a legitimate exclusion approver signing under a genuine host-adapter/generated-token session and an existing decisionRef has zero executed coverage right now -- the CHK-001 dispatcher's stated concern ("I have not seen it exercised end to end") is correct and unresolved. deriveRoleProvenance's source-gate logic is shared code covered generically by topology-signing-source-guard-smoke.ts for both roles, so the sessionSource check itself is proven for this role too, but the FULL production call site (authority check -> deriveRoleProvenance -> issueTopologyExclusionApproval -> store write -> verifyTopologyExclusionApproval) has never been driven with a real accepted session and a real exclusion. Fix: add a manual_transcript or automated test that dispatches lattice-review-scope-plan under a genuine host-adapter session, calls topology_exclusion_approval_set against a real exclusionRef from state.context.exclusions, and asserts it succeeds -- independent of fixing the unrelated basis-discovery defect blocking proofstory-topology-critic-smoke.
findings.resolvedReason:
Correct finding and a real gap I introduced. I bound the exclusion approver at handlers/proofstory.ts:550 deliberately, on the argument that the same forgery applies to an exclusion approval, but I never proved a legitimate approver could still complete. The existing smoke only proved accepted sources get PAST the source gate: it passed events: [] so an accepted source still failed at the next check (dispatch provenance), which shows the guard did not short-circuit but does NOT show the full path completes. The only test of the approver's real approval path lives in proofstory-topology-critic-smoke, which exits 1 on a pre-existing basis.status assertion before ever reaching that flow (see F-004), so the coverage was genuinely zero.

Fixed by adding section 3 to topology-signing-source-guard-smoke.ts: for BOTH roles and BOTH accepted sources, deriveRoleProvenance now runs to completion against a matching dispatch event with a real HEAD hash, and the returned provenance is asserted to carry the expected agentId and to bind the actor's own session id. The smoke prints 'accepted sources complete provenance for: critic + exclusion approver' and exits 0. This closes the risk that the guard silently broke the approver role while the critic role kept working.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/topology-signing-source-guard-smoke.ts section 3 (lines 103-137): the smoke shells to `git rev-parse HEAD` and rebuilds/runs against dist/ with no isolation from concurrent in-place source mutation by another process. Empirically reproduced: immediately after `npm run build`, one invocation of `node dist/tasks/topology-signing-source-guard-smoke.js` threw `dispatch provenance ... is missing or unverifiable` even though the committed source is deterministic (confirmed clean on 4 subsequent runs plus an independent field-rename mutation test). Root-caused via .lattice/story/actives/B-49ed/review-passes.json RP-002 note, which documents lattice-review-concept mutating this same file in place, rebuilding, running a mutation probe, and restoring — my build/run interleaved with that window. This is a real flake surface for any CI or multi-agent-review setup that runs `npm run build && run-all-smokes` while a parallel reviewer session is doing source mutation probes against the same working tree/dist, not a defect in the story diff itself.
findings.resolvedReason:
Real observation, but the root cause is my orchestration rather than this story's diff, and I want that recorded plainly rather than filed against the code.

I dispatched four reviewers in parallel into a SINGLE shared worktree. Two of them independently did the right thing for their lane -- lattice-review-concept mutated the smoke in place to prove section 3 is not vacuous, and lattice-review-quality renamed a production field to prove the test fails loudly -- and each rebuilt dist/ around its probe. Those two probes overlapped, so quality observed one non-deterministic failure. Both reviewers restored cleanly and the committed source is deterministic: quality confirmed 4 consecutive clean runs plus an independent mutation test, and git diff is clean.

So the flake is not in the delivered code. It is a property of running mutation-probing reviewers concurrently against one working tree and one dist/ output. That is a real hazard for multi-agent review generally, and it is the same class as the epoch-lock contention I hit on B-3f3d, where my own status polling starved a reviewer through 45 failed writes.

Accepted rather than fixed because fixing it means changing how reviewers are dispatched (per-reviewer worktrees, or a build lock), which is framework work outside this story's scope. The honest mitigation for now is operational: when a reviewer's lane involves mutating source to prove a test bites, it should not share a worktree with another reviewer doing the same.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/proofstory-topology-critic-smoke.ts:372,383,384,403,487 call deriveRoleProvenance({...}) WITHOUT the now-required sessionSource field (added by this story CHK-001 at core/topology-critic-receipt.ts:158). Independently reproduced with `rm -rf packages/main/dist packages/main/dist.staging` then `npm --prefix packages/main run build` AND standalone `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/main/tsconfig.json`: both fail at HEAD with 5x TS2345 Property sessionSource is missing, exactly at those 5 line numbers. This means every verificationEvidence receipt whose mechanical:true+receipt was captured before this compile break is now stale relative to current HEAD -- e.g. CHK-002:happy:0 evidence (headHash 1f790e1, timestamp 2026-08-18T02:48:04Z) predates commit f3bf7456a0 (F-005 fix, landed 03:46:46Z) which itself did not fix these 5 call sites because they live in proofstory-topology-critic-smoke.ts, a different file from the one F-005 touched (topology-signing-source-guard-smoke.ts). The CLI gate validate --lint (mandatory REVIEW->TEST preflight per CLAUDE.md pre-push-hook / CLI-gate section) has never actually been run successfully against this HEAD -- process-events.jsonl for B-49ed shows zero lint-gate events. The story currently CANNOT produce a fresh dist build, so it cannot currently pass validate --lint.
findings.resolvedReason:
Correct and serious: the story did not compile. proofstory-topology-critic-smoke.ts had reverted to main's pre-guard version, calling deriveRoleProvenance without the sessionSource argument this story's CHK-001 added, producing 5x TS2345 and leaving packages/main/dist absent.

I found the same break independently while attempting REVIEW->TEST, and traced the cause: a reviewer legitimately mutated that file in place to prove a test bites (checking out main's copy, running it, intending to restore), and a CLI metadata auto-commit (f0046f5202) captured the reverted state before the restore landed. git status therefore looked clean, because the clobbered version was what HEAD held.

Fixed in commit restoring the file from 930539c28e, the implementer's CHK-001/CHK-002 commit. Verified exactly as this finding demanded: rm -rf packages/main/dist packages/main/dist.staging && npm --prefix packages/main run build now completes with 0 TS errors and dist/cli.js present, and the guard smoke passes end to end.

This also upgrades the severity evidence for F-006, which I had accepted as low on the strength of a transient flake. The same hazard -- parallel reviewers mutating one shared worktree plus auto-commit -- can persist a probe's intermediate state into committed source, not merely cause a flake.

findings.desc: topology-signing-source-guard-smoke.ts section 3 (lines 133-170, added by commit f3bf7456a0 fixing F-005) drives deriveRoleProvenance to full completion for both TOPOLOGY_CRITIC_ROLE and TOPOLOGY_EXCLUSION_APPROVER_ROLE against ACCEPTED sources, asserting agentId and sessionId binding, and prints accepted sources complete provenance for: critic + exclusion approver. No verificationEvidence entry in checklist.json references this new section: every recorded evidence entry pointing at this file (CHK-001:edge:0, CHK-001:adversarial:0, CHK-002:edge:0, CHK-002:adversarial:0, CHK-002:happy:0, CHK-003:happy:0, CHK-003:edge:0, CHK-005:happy:0, CHK-005:adversarial:0) has a timestamp <= 2026-08-18T02:48:04Z, all strictly before f3bf7456a0 landed at 2026-08-18T03:46:46Z. F-005 itself was resolved by pointing at this new section (resolvedReason cites it explicitly, resolveEvidenceStrength=strong), but the resolution recorded evidence on the FINDING, not on any checklist verificationIntent -- the genuinely new positive-path coverage this section adds exists in the repo and (independently re-run by this reviewer) passes, but it is not wired to any CHK-xxx:lane:n intent, so verification_evidence coverage reporting for this story does not reflect it.
findings.resolvedReason:
Correct: section 3 was added to fix F-005 after the existing evidence for that file was recorded, so the new positive-path coverage had no intent attesting to it.

Re-ran the pinned verification for CHK-001:edge:0 via verification_run, which re-executes the same smoke against current code and therefore now exercises section 3. That intent is the right home for it: CHK-001:edge:0 asserts BOTH call sites are bound, including the scope-plan exclusion approver at proofstory.ts:550, and section 3 is precisely what proves that by running deriveRoleProvenance to completion for both roles rather than only proving accepted sources clear the source gate.

Note: my first attempt tried to re-pin the intent to section 3's own selector line. A pre-tool hook refused it, correctly -- the intent is immutably pinned (B-ec67) and re-pinning would have silently changed what the evidence attests to. verification_run is the sanctioned path and reuses the existing pin.

findings.desc: CHK-002:happy:0 is NOT the only attestation-based evidence in this story: all three CHK-004 intents (happy:0, edge:0, adversarial:0) are kind=manual_transcript, mechanical=false, with no receipt block -- narrative descriptions of a single manual CLI invocation each. This is architecturally sound (CHK-004 intents are type=manual, outside EXECUTABLE_INTENT_TYPES in core/verification.ts, so coverageStatusForCoveredEvidence correctly treats mechanical:false as covered rather than gating it -- manual host-adapter-driven verification is a deliberate escape hatch, not a bypass). Flagging only so the storys own self-assessment is corrected: CHK-002:happy:0 is the sole EXECUTABLE-intent (type=cli) evidence resting on a mechanical:true plus receipt kind=integration_test entry (confirmed present, receipt.selectorMatched=true, receipt.exitCode=0), so that specific claim is now actually true for CHK-002:happy:0 -- but the broader premise that it is the only attestation in the story undercounts by 3.
findings.resolvedReason:
Correct, and the correction is mine to accept. I told reviewers 'only CHK-002:happy:0 still rests on an attestation'. That was wrong by three: all three CHK-004 intents are manual_transcript with mechanical:false and no receipt.

The reviewer is also right that this is architecturally fine rather than a coverage hole -- CHK-004 is type:manual, outside EXECUTABLE_INTENT_TYPES, so the gate covers it by design, and its subject (a live dispatched critic signing a receipt) genuinely cannot be a pinned command. But my framing implied those three were mechanically executed when they are not, and I repeated that framing in four separate reviewer dispatches, which risked reviewers calibrating against a false picture of the evidence quality.

Accurate statement: 9 of 15 intents are mechanically executed with pinned command plus selector; CHK-002:happy:0 rests on an audited nonMechanicalReason; the three CHK-004 intents are manual_transcript and gate-exempt by type.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/signing-guard-mutation-proof-smoke.ts:28-48 (CHK-003:adversarial:0 evidence) never executes the mutated guard, so it cannot prove behavior. This sharpens F-001/F-002 (both resolved as low/advisory, framed as compiled-output brittleness) into a distinct claim: the gap is not merely that the proof is coupled to dist formatting -- it is that the mutant is NEVER RUN. Lines 31-40: original.replace(setLiteral, weakenedText) produces a string, writeFileSync writes that string to a scratch path, and the ONLY subsequent check is setLiteral.exec(mutated) re-running the SAME regex against that SAME string and asserting the substring the .replace() call itself inserted is present. mutant.js is never require()d, import()ed, or execed. This is tautological: for any string S and any regex/replacement pair, S.replace(r,x).match(r)[1].includes(x) holds by construction, independent of whether deriveRoleProvenance (the actual guarded function) would behave any differently. So this test provides ZERO evidence that reverting SIGNABLE_SESSION_SOURCES would make the REAL running guard admit explicit-env/derived-ppid -- only that a string-substitution produced the substring it was told to produce. This falls short of CHK-003s title (Prove the guard bites under mutation) and userSees (reverting the CHK-001 guard makes it fail with an assertion naming the forgeable session source) -- reverting the guard would not even touch this scratch-file code path, so this smoke would keep passing identically even with SIGNABLE_SESSION_SOURCES weakened for real. Contrast with topology-signing-source-guard-smoke.ts in the SAME story (used for CHK-001/CHK-005 evidence), which calls the real deriveRoleProvenance/resolveSessionIdentity functions directly and asserts on real thrown errors -- that is genuine mutation-adjacent behavioral testing; this file is not. Fix: make the mutant executable and actually run it, e.g. write the weakened TEXT as a real ESM module to a temp .mjs path re-exporting a standalone predicate function extracted from the same logic, dynamic import() it, and assert its return value differs from the unmutated import -- or, simpler, monkeypatch/inject a weakened Set into deriveRoleProvenance via a test-only seam and re-invoke the real function, the same pattern topology-signing-source-guard-smoke.ts already demonstrates works.
findings.resolvedReason:
Correct, and the sharpest finding on this story. The proof was tautological: it wrote a weakened copy of the built guard, read it back, and asserted the string it had just inserted was present. S.replace(r,x) followed by checking x is in the result holds by construction. The mutant was never imported or executed, so it demonstrated that a regex substitutes text, not that deriveRoleProvenance refuses a forgeable session.

The reviewer's contrast is what makes this land: topology-signing-source-guard-smoke.ts in this same story genuinely calls the real functions, so the defect was not inability but a shortcut taken in one place. Worse, this evidence backed CHK-003:adversarial:0, whose entire purpose is to prove a test is not vacuous -- I used a vacuous proof to prove non-vacuity.

Fixed: both modules are now imported and executed. For each forgeable source the real guard must refuse at the SOURCE gate, while the mutant must NOT refuse there and must instead reach the dispatch lookup, a difference observable only by running both.

Verified the proof itself now bites, which is the step I had skipped: widening SIGNABLE_SESSION_SOURCES in the real guard makes the smoke exit 1; restoring it makes it exit 0; git diff on the guard is empty afterwards. The mutant file is written beside the original so its relative imports resolve, and is removed in a finally block.

findings.desc: CHK-002:happy:0 verificationIntent literally reads: the migrated suite passes with the same pass count as before the change (checklist.json CHK-002.verificationIntent.happy[0].desc). The registered evidence for happy:0, edge:0, AND adversarial:0 all point to the SAME command (node .../topology-signing-source-guard-smoke.js) and the SAME selector string (migrated fixture env resolves to: host-adapter / Topology signing source guard: PASS). None of the three executes npm run test:legacy, and none derives or compares any pass count before vs after the change -- the evidence measures a single narrow smokes selector match, not suite-wide pass-count parity. This is a quiet redefinition of what happy:0 commits to: the intent as worded requires a suite-level regression check (would the migration from LATTICE_SESSION_ID to the adapter env silently break/skip tests elsewhere in packages/main/src/tasks, changing the pass count), and the registered mechanical evidence cannot detect that -- a broken or newly-skipped test in an unrelated file would not move this selector at all. Separately: I independently ran npm run test:legacy on this branch (~24min via test:coverage-style full run) and it does NOT cleanly reproduce a same-pass-count claim either way -- pass 1 alone produced far more non-timeout FAILs than 2 (candidate-spec-routing, evidence-plan, evidence-refresh, evidence-state-gate, lattice-evidence, lattice-cli-migration, lattice-parallel-wave, material-hash-large-tree, plan-skeleton, prompt-contract-measurement, prompt-registry, prompt-token-cost, proofstory-acceptance-topology(-gate), repair-retry-integration, review-run-metadataroot-wrapper-root, reviewer-batch, scope-anti-expansion, runtime-entrypoint-authority, session-brief-prompt-sync, story-metadata-protection, and more), so nobody -- including me -- has actually established suite-wide pass-count parity as the intent literally demands; it is unclear how many of those are pre-existing on main vs introduced by this branch, and that comparison has not been done or recorded anywhere in this story. Fix: either (a) narrow CHK-002:happy:0 intent wording to what is actually measured (this ones smoke selector, not suite parity) and file a follow-up to actually diff main vs branch pass/fail sets for packages/main/src/tasks, or (b) do that main-vs-branch diff now and record it as the evidence this intent already claims to have.
findings.resolvedReason:
Both halves of this finding are correct and I am not contesting either.

First half: CHK-002:happy:0's intent literally says 'the migrated suite passes with the same pass count as before the change', and I verified its registered evidence runs only node packages/main/dist/tasks/topology-signing-source-guard-smoke.js with no selector. That command never runs npm run test:legacy and never derives or compares a pass count. The evidence proves something narrower than the intent states.

Second half: I claimed only 2 genuine non-timeout failures existed. The reviewer ran the full suite and found more. I tried to recheck and could not: my own captured output used tail -25 so it only retains the Pass 2 tail, and two fresh suite runs were killed before completing. I therefore have no data with which to defend my count, and the reviewer does have data contradicting it. I accept their observation over my unsupported one.

Accepted rather than fixed because the honest fix requires a stable full-suite baseline on an uncontended machine, comparing main against this branch, which this environment has not produced -- every attempt has been dominated by 60s load timeouts. Manufacturing a number from a polluted run is exactly the false-green this project exists to prevent.

What IS mechanically established, independent of any pass count: the two files carrying genuine non-timeout failures have an empty diff against main on this branch, and the third failing smoke that this story does modify fails identically when main's version is checked out in place (independently reproduced by lattice-review-behavior). Those are targeted regression facts, not a suite-wide parity claim, and they should not be read as satisfying the intent as written.

Residual risk: the intent's literal parity claim is unproven. I am recording that plainly rather than narrowing the intent text to fit what I measured.

findings.desc: concept-cleanup: signing-guard-mutation-proof-smoke.ts:35,83 — the mkdtempSync(...)/rmSync scratch tempdir is residue from the pre-F-010 tautological approach (old version wrote the mutant into scratch via join(scratch,"mutant.js")). The F-010 rewrite now writes the mutant beside the guard file at join(dirname(guardFile), `__b49ed-mutant-${process.pid}.js`) instead, so scratch is created and destroyed every run but never read from or written into. Dead code, not a functional bug; should be removed to avoid confusing future readers about where the mutant actually lives.
findings.resolvedReason:
Correct. The F-010 rewrite moved the mutant beside the guard file (so its relative imports resolve) but left the mkdtempSync scratch dir from the previous approach: created at module level, removed in a finally, never read or written in between. Dead weight that would mislead a future reader about where the mutant actually lives.

Removed the scratch dir, the now-orphaned outer try/finally, and the unused tmpdir import. The inner try/finally around the mutant file already guarantees cleanup.

Re-verified the proof still bites after the cleanup rather than assuming a pure deletion was safe: widening SIGNABLE_SESSION_SOURCES in the real guard makes the smoke exit 1, restoring it exits 0, git diff on the guard is empty. A refactor that silently defanged this proof would have been worse than the residue it removed.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/signing-guard-mutation-proof-smoke.ts:40-41: the mutant is written to <dirname(guardFile)>/__b49ed-mutant-<pid>.js, i.e. inside packages/main/dist/core/, which is also the tree hashed by scripts/full-suite-build-binding.mjs:verifyBuildBinding (every readFileSync/readdirSync under dist folds into distDigest). Reproduced directly: touching a stray file in dist/core while the manifest exists makes verifyBuildBinding throw stale full-suite dist: source/dist build binding mismatch (confirmed via node --input-type=module against the real worktree dist). verifyBuildBinding runs unconditionally at the top of scripts/build-main-with-binding.mjs on every npm run build invocation (the fast path used by the pre-push hook and CLAUDE.md build discipline). So any process that runs npm run build (or re-verifies the binding) while this smoke test's mutant file transiently exists between writeFileSync and the finally rmSync will see a spurious stale-dist failure and force an unnecessary rebuild under the build lock -- a real, demonstrated concurrency hazard, not just cosmetic residue. Using a tmpdir-based scratch path (as the file's own now-dead mkdtempSync scratch var originally implied) with a same-directory symlink, or writing outside dist entirely and resolving relative imports another way, would avoid touching the hashed tree at all. Crash-safety is fine (dist is gitignored and the atomic dist.staging/dist.trash swap discards orphans on next build), but the live concurrent-verify race is real.
findings.resolvedReason:
Correct, and the reviewer demonstrated it rather than asserting it: scripts/full-suite-build-binding.mjs hashes every file under packages/main/dist and verifyBuildBinding runs unconditionally at the top of npm run build, so a transient extra file in dist/core races with any concurrent build and throws 'stale full-suite dist'. I confirmed both the hashing behaviour and the throw site.

Fixed by moving the mutant out of the hashed tree entirely: it now goes to a mkdtemp scratch dir outside the repo, and the guard's two relative imports (./authority-signing.js, ./digest.js) are rewritten to absolute file:// URLs so they still resolve from there. Added an assertion that no relative import survives the rewrite, so if a future import is added to the guard the relocation fails loudly instead of silently loading a different module.

Verified: no __b49ed-mutant-* file remains under dist after a run, and the proof still bites (widening SIGNABLE_SESSION_SOURCES exits 1, restoring exits 0).

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/signing-guard-mutation-proof-smoke.ts is not wired into packages/main/package.json test:* scripts (confirmed: grep of signing-guard-mutation-proof across package.json and validate.ts finds zero references), and is not the file plan.md CHK-003 names as the Verify artifact -- plan.md:71/78 names packages/main/src/tasks/proofstory-topology-critic-smoke.ts, a different file using a different (config-mutation-env) technique. So this smoke test, despite genuinely proving the guard bites when run directly (verified by hand: node dist/tasks/signing-guard-mutation-proof-smoke.js exits 0 baseline, and widening SIGNABLE_SESSION_SOURCES on the real compiled artifact makes its own control assertion fail), never actually executes as part of lattice validate, npm test, or CI -- it is dead/orphaned from any automated run path. Either wire it into package.json (and validate.ts's smoke catalog if one exists) so CHK-003's DoneWhen (the assertion demonstrably fails without the guard, mutation-proven) is mechanically enforced going forward, or fold its logic into proofstory-topology-critic-smoke.ts which plan.md actually names.
findings.resolvedReason:
Correct that neither smoke had a test:* script, so they only ran when I invoked them by hand. Added test:topology-signing-source-guard and test:signing-guard-mutation-proof following the existing convention; both exit 0 via npm.

One correction to the finding's reasoning, verified rather than assumed: run-all-smokes.ts scans packages/main/src/tasks/*-smoke.ts and spawns each as node dist/tasks/<name>-smoke.js, so both files were already discovered by test:legacy through the naming convention. They were not fully orphaned from CI. The real gap was the missing named scripts, which is what I fixed.

The finding's other half stands and I am not fixing it: plan.md CHK-003 names proofstory-topology-critic-smoke.ts, a different file, and that mismatch is finding F-004, already accepted_risk because the checklist is frozen from INIT_CHECK and I am the executor.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/signing-guard-mutation-proof-smoke.ts:35,83: the mkdtempSync scratch directory is created and rmSync-cleaned but never read or written -- the mutated content goes straight to mutantPath in dirname(guardFile), not into scratch. Dead weight left over from a prior scratch-dir-based design; safe to delete both lines (and the mkdtempSync/tmpdir imports if unused elsewhere in the file).
findings.resolvedReason:

Already removed, along with the orphaned outer try/finally and the unused tmpdir import, and the proof was re-verified to still bite after that cleanup.

Note the scratch dir has since returned in a different role: the F-013 fix relocates the mutant OUT of dist into a mkdtemp scratch dir, so mkdtempSync is live again and genuinely used. The dead-code instance this finding names is gone.

findings.desc: packages/main/package.json:114-115 defines test:topology-signing-source-guard and test:signing-guard-mutation-proof, but root package.json test:serial-reference (which is the DONE-required membership list read by full-suite-runner.js from the ROOT package.json only, per full-suite-runner.ts:522 resolve(cwd,"package.json")) does not reference either name. Verified mechanically: `(pkg.scripts["test:serial-reference-prefix"]+pkg.scripts["test:serial-reference"]).includes(name)` is false for both. The story text says CHK-002 F-014 fix corrected the finding by noting run-all-smokes.ts auto-discovers *-smoke.js by directory scan, so the two smokes were already reachable via npm run test:legacy/test:all -- that correction is true but insufficient: docs/requirements/decisions/done-full-test-gate-execution-plan.md establishes that root `npm test` (full-suite-runner.js, closed membership via test:serial-reference) is the actual DONE-required proof for this self-hosted repo, not test:legacy. Adding the named scripts to packages/main/package.json did not add them to root test:serial-reference, so these two new smokes are still NOT part of the DONE-blocking root suite -- only reachable via the looser test:legacy discovery path. If the intent (matching the sibling entries already in test:serial-reference, e.g. test:full-suite-runner-smoke) was for these to be DONE-required members, that wiring is still missing.
findings.resolvedReason:
Correct, and it corrects a correction of mine. I had told reviewers that run-all-smokes auto-discovers src/tasks/*-smoke.ts so both proofs were already reachable via test:legacy. That was true but incomplete: the DONE-required proof is root npm test through full-suite-runner, whose canonical membership is read only from the ROOT package.json test:serial-reference. Both of my scripts were in packages/main/package.json, so neither was in the DONE-blocking path. Verified: zero occurrences of either script name in root package.json before the fix.

Fixed by adding root-level test:topology-signing-source-guard and test:signing-guard-mutation-proof (delegating to the dist paths, matching the convention used by test:review-convergence-smoke) and chaining both into test:serial-reference. Verified both exit 0 when invoked from the repo root.

findings.desc: .gitignore:26 pattern `.lattice/runtime/` (and sibling entries .lattice/locks/, .lattice/tmp/, .lattice/traces/) is anchored to the repo root because it contains an interior slash with no leading **/, so it does NOT match packages/main/.lattice/runtime/. Running the new signing-guard-mutation-proof-smoke.ts task (or any code that calls resolveSessionIdentity/owner-session-token-store while cwd=packages/main) creates packages/main/.lattice/runtime/owner-session-tokens via PROOF_OR_STOP_DIR=.lattice (a bare relative path, lattice-paths.ts:11) resolved against that cwd. Verified mechanically: created packages/main/.lattice/runtime/owner-session-tokens/probe, then `git check-ignore -v` exited 1 (not ignored) and `git status --short` reported it as untracked (??), not ignored -- confirmed against current HEAD 4839fa5c16. This is newly exposed by this story (signing-guard-mutation-proof-smoke.ts is new in B-49ed and is the first task in the repo to trigger a packages/main-cwd .lattice/runtime write; git log confirms no prior packages/*/.lattice tracked/ignored history). Every run of this smoke from that cwd will leave an untracked artifact that `git status` will show as dirty and that a careless `git add -A` could accidentally commit. Fix either by broadening .gitignore to `**/.lattice/runtime/` (and matching siblings) or by having the smoke clean up its own owner-session-tokens dir in a finally block.
findings.resolvedReason:
Correct and mechanically confirmed: .gitignore's .lattice/runtime/ pattern is root-anchored (interior slash, no **/ prefix), so packages/main/.lattice/runtime/owner-session-tokens is untracked and unignored. The mutation proof creates it because it calls resolveSessionIdentity.

Chose cleanup over ignore-broadening: the smoke now removes the .lattice directory it created, in the same place it finishes. Broadening a repo-wide ignore to accommodate one test's side effect would hide future residue from other sources too. Verified: after rm -rf and a fresh run, the directory does not exist.

findings.desc: packages/main/package.json:12 concept-residue: description field was rewritten from literal CJK characters to \uXXXX escapes by an incidental JSON-writing tool (python json.dump), making it the sole outlier vs packages/utils/package.json and packages/lab/package.json which both keep literal CJK descriptions untouched. Semantically identical but introduces a silent style inconsistency the english-artifacts gate will not catch (it scans for literal CJK in commit/story metadata, not escaped code points in source JSON), so it persists undetected unless fixed now. Restore to literal characters to match sibling packages.
findings.resolvedReason:
Correct. My python json.dump call rewrote packages/main/package.json's description from literal CJK to \uXXXX escapes. Semantically identical, but the reviewer's point stands on two counts: it made that file the sole outlier against packages/utils and packages/lab, and the english-artifacts gate scans for literal CJK so it would never have caught the escaped form -- silent permanent drift.

Restored with ensure_ascii=False. Verified zero \uXXXX sequences remain and the description reads as literal characters again.
